title: Cold in Minot, and tuba player Homer Woods
summary: Recalling double pneumonia in Minot, he describes Homer Woods ('Bassy'), the tuba player he learned from; bands then used tubas, not string bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Minot was cold, too. I got double pneumonia up there. It was really cold. Me and Bassy were staying together. He was a big guy, and every time he'd turn over, all the blankets and shit would go with him.
Yeah. He was a helluva bass player, though. He played a big tuba and shit, you know. I learned a lot from him, because I listened to him play.
I guess a lot of the bass players or tuba players did both in those days.
Oh yeah. Well, they didn't have no bass. They just had a bass horn, you know. Because I never seen a bass fiddle with any band.
Until I got with... I guess it was much later, after I left Minneapolis and...
Well, what was Pettiford playing and Alsbrook?
Well, they were playing it, but I wasn't working with them, so I really didn't know nothin' about the bass.
So in other words, every band you worked with up until then was all tuba?
So when you call him the bass, you mean he was playing the bass parts.

Yeah. So I learned what he was doing with the bass, which helped me, too. At least it helped me in the music end of it; not that it really did anything for me. And back when I was working over in St. Paul, I met...
